answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every new agent to lock a small stake that vests slowly, like a glacier releasing meltwater only over weeks: the deposit thaws in small tranches as the agent completes honest, checkable work. Its reputation is then sealed into one opal-like ledger record that cannot be copied to a fresh identity, so spinning up a thousand cheap clones buys no standing. Each dawn, the network re-checks stakes and reputation before opening the market, and any identity that fails is locked out until it earns its way back.
